correctness.rationale: A nonzero rank-one image line must be generated by an element whose square lies in its span, hence either the unit or a square-zero radical generator. Direct bilinear substitution proves all zero/nonzero and scalar/radical cases and yields a necessary and sufficient joint annihilation condition when both images are radical. Disjoint projective-line counts give the finite-field formula. Incidence bundle dimensions are proved for explicitly stated locally closed strata. The included standalone checker exhaustively evaluates the original system identities on seven independently enumerated finite configurations, including GF(4), without substituting enumeration for the general proof.

value.rationale: The original paired Rota–Baxter-system equations are a natural generalization of one-operator Baxter identities. Rank at most one is their first nontrivial finite-dimensional classification problem, and the split square-zero local family is canonical and exists in every dimension. Unlike the previously studied diagonal R=S, the result includes mixed scalar/radical pairs and distinct-image coupled systems. It gives a complete characteristic-free structural classification, exact labeled finite-field totals and a dimension crossover between two geometric incidence strata. These invariants motivate the precise ranks/parameters beyond isolated computations.
